mbm-0568.clue: My robot borrows the light from my desk.
mbm-0568.quote: I cut a clear panel for the model's chest and slipped a piece of old red sweet wrapper behind it. When I turn my lamp, the little engine looks like it's waking up from a long nap.

mbm-0569.clue: My favorite photo is still damp around the edges.
mbm-0569.quote: I took portraits at our family picnic just as it started to rain. My brother held an umbrella over the camera and got soaked himself. I used the last frame on him smiling under the dripping trees.

mbm-0570.clue: The bell tower has a peppermint ledge.
mbm-0570.quote: We used to leave peppermints on the sill for the long practice. The captain rang my first perfect change, reached up and placed one mint in my palm without a word. It tasted like a medal.

mbm-0571.clue: My first seam can open a bottle.
mbm-0571.quote: I stitched my uncle a sturdy apron with a reinforced loop for his bottle opener. The loop is a bit crooked. He says it points the guests straight toward the lemonade.

mbm-0572.clue: One of my robot's boots is a letterbox.
mbm-0572.quote: I lost a tiny access panel, so I painted the opening bright red. Now my nephew folds messages smaller than a fingernail and posts them to the pilot. The robot has a much busier social life than I do.

mbm-0573.clue: I race a different clock on rainy mornings.
mbm-0573.quote: Water falls from a bent gutter onto the window of our little corner shop. I run my short loop before the clear patch in the glass fills up again. The shopkeeper moves the fruit so I can see my time.

mbm-0574.clue: My leather pencil case has a worn smile.
mbm-0574.quote: I made a simple roll for my drawing pencils. Every time I open it the leather bends along the same curved line. After five years it looks like the case is glad to see the paper.

mbm-0575.clue: Our favorite scene has six different skies.
mbm-0575.quote: At anime club we copied one background in chalk, but each of us chose a different hour for the sky. I got deep purple dusk. We lined the drawings up and watched a whole day pass without pressing play.

mbm-0576.clue: I made a tiny runway out of crumbs.
mbm-0576.quote: At breakfast after my first parachute jump I used two crusts and a line of crumbs to show my father where I landed. He moved the jam jar over to be the sun. The whole table joined the flight.

mbm-0577.clue: I got to hear what the museum keeps in the dark.
mbm-0577.quote: The museum offered a listening tour one rainy Saturday. A curator turned an old hand-cranked music box with its lid closed, then lifted the lid for the second verse. I drew the same little tune twice, once in pencil and once in bright orange.

mbm-0578.clue: My helmet has a crooked constellation.
mbm-0578.quote: Each trip down the river leaves a little scratch on my old helmet. I joined three of them with removable tape after a good run. My friend saw a fish. I saw our whole boat riding a wave.

mbm-0579.clue: My window tree grows birds in winter.
mbm-0579.quote: I cut a bare tree from red paper and taped it to the glass. Every time a friend visited I cut one little bird for a branch. By the new year the paper tree could have sung down the street.

mbm-0580.clue: My gym clock runs on soup.
mbm-0580.quote: I train in the back room of my parents' cafe. When the soup lid starts rattling I know my final set is due. Dad always saves me the heel of the loaf and a bowl as heavy as my lightest plate.

mbm-0581.clue: I borrowed the color of a wet cobble.
mbm-0581.quote: I was painting the market when a stallholder washed one patch of pavement. Suddenly all the fruit colors shone upside down on that stone. I turned my canvas over and painted the reflection first.

mbm-0582.clue: My pilot climbs aboard with a paper ladder.
mbm-0582.quote: I folded a ladder from a bus ticket for the tiny pilot of my model robot. The ticket was from the day I bought the kit. Even the trip to the shop ended up inside the scene.

mbm-0583.clue: The floor tells me when I've hurried.
mbm-0583.quote: Our dojo mats meet in one narrow blue seam. When I rush my turn my heel catches it. I can feel the difference between getting there fast and arriving with my feet under me.

mbm-0584.clue: The little creek gets a postcard every year.
mbm-0584.quote: I draw one bend from my canoe each spring. Last year my daughter spotted a turtle I'd left out. She added a tiny green oval on the log, and that became everyone's favorite part of the card.

mbm-0585.clue: My airplane notebook has an orange horizon.
mbm-0585.quote: At the grass airfield I prop a slice of orange on my lunchbox and line its curve up with a wing in the distance. It started as a joke, but I drew the sweetest little biplane over it.

mbm-0586.clue: Our most valuable property is a cardboard doghouse.
mbm-0586.quote: I built a doghouse for the corner square on our board. The roof lifts up and holds the bank. My little niece insists on knocking before anyone can take change.

mbm-0587.clue: The mirror only sees half our turn.
mbm-0587.quote: My ballroom partner and I rehearse in an old hall with a narrow mirror. First I vanish out of view, then she does. When both our faces finally land in the glass together we know the turn is right.

mbm-0588.clue: My card sleeves have one green thumbprint.
mbm-0588.quote: I was potting herbs before our fantasy-card night and marked a new sleeve with green paint from the pot. The mark sits behind a forest creature. Everyone thinks I did that enchanted thumbprint on purpose.

mbm-0589.clue: I made a quilt from wrong numbers.
mbm-0589.quote: My granddad saved shirts from teams he never played for because the numbers on them were misprinted. I cut the numbers into squares. They add up to a truly terrible score and a very warm blanket.

mbm-0590.clue: I turn the page at the sound of a spoon.
mbm-0590.quote: My little cousin likes stories but reads slowly. During tea we share a book and he taps his spoon on the saucer when he's ready. We got through a whole mystery in thirteen cups.

mbm-0591.clue: I chalk the score on a driftwood bat.
mbm-0591.quote: We use one retired beach-cricket bat for keeping score. At the end of a match everybody signs the handle in wet sand. By morning the handle is clean but I can usually remember who hit what.

mbm-0592.clue: Our quilt has a lighthouse that actually turns.
mbm-0592.quote: I sewed a yellow fabric beam to a button at the top of my quilted lighthouse. My brother can swing it across the waves. He checks the toy ferry has made it home before he'll let anyone fold the quilt.
